install_tell: docker run -p 2379:2379 -p 2380:2380 quay.io/coreos/etcd:latest — standalone deploy, no k8s apiserver co-located (k8s-embedded etcd is a separate  category, do not duplicate)
misconfig_patterns: auth subsystem is OFF by default until 'etcdctl auth enable' is explicitly run — full read/write with zero credentials out of the box
client-cert-auth (mTLS) not required by default — plaintext HTTP client port reachable
v2 API /v2/keys/?recursive=true dumps entire keyspace in one unauth GET
v3 API grpc-gateway /v3/kv/range with base64 empty-string key + range_end=\\0 dumps entire v3 keyspace unauth
/metrics exposes Prometheus stats incl. cluster member count, leader changes — recon without touching keyspace

active_probe.false_positive_check: GET /version must return JSON with both 'etcdserver' and 'etcdcluster' keys — unique to etcd's version endpoint, unauth by design

deployment_tells: POST-shaped grpc-gateway GET :2379/v3/kv/range (base64 key='', range_end='\\0') -> full v3 keyspace dump
GET :2379/metrics -> etcd_server_has_leader, etcd_server_is_leader, member list -> cluster topology without keyspace read
pivot_paths: keyspace dump often contains service-discovery entries: DB connection strings, service URLs, sometimes plaintext credentials stored by naive app configs

if co-located with k8s (hand off — different category) keyspace holds cluster secrets; standalone etcd used by Kafka/Cadence/Vitess/TiKV/CockroachDB for coordination-only metadata, lower blast radius but still config/topology leak
cross-check: instances also answering on 2380 (peer port) confirm multi-node ensemble -> higher-value target (more members' data reachable via a single unauth node)
vulnerabilities: CVE-2018-1002105 (unrelated k8s apiserver, noted for cross-category awareness)
No CVE required — 'no-auth-by-default' is a design-default finding, not a bug
